lesson.title: Song-style: Back In Black
lesson.one_line_promise: Play a 3-chord loop inspired by "Back In Black".
objectives: Form Em, G, D (each verified by chord-theory-check.js)
Loop Em – G – D cleanly at 70 bpm
Note: this is an original practice progression using the same chords — not the published song

chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

Em.name: E minor
Em.note: Verified deterministically by chord-theory-check.js (2026-08-08) as E B G.

G.name: G major
G.note: Verified deterministically by chord-theory-check.js (2026-08-08) as G B D.

D.name: D major
D.note: Verified deterministically by chord-theory-check.js (2026-08-08) as D A F#.

exercises.name: The shapes: Em, G, D
exercises.purpose: Learn each chord in the loop as its own clean voicing.
exercises.coaching: These are the chords behind "Back In Black". Learn each one slow and clean — the app verifies every fingering for you.

exercises.name: Loop the progression
exercises.purpose: Strum Em – G – D in time, one bar each.
exercises.coaching: One bar each, round and round. Find the loop by ear — that is the whole trick. Keep it clean before you speed it up.

exercises.name: 1-minute changes (loop pairs)
exercises.purpose: Count your weakest change inside the loop.
exercises.coaching: The hardest change in this loop is Em to G. Drill it for a minute — the app remembers it for spaced review.
